standard_prerequisites: tor amplitude of an object of the derived category of modules
etale neighbourhoods U to X with affine U, quasi-compact separated by quasi-separatedness, and pushforward preserving quasi-coherence
the etale pull-push splitting lemma exhibiting a module as a direct summand of j^*j_*G
the comparison of the derived category of quasi-coherent modules on a space with the small etale derived category and flatness of the localization functor
the schemes version of the tor-amplitude criterion
core_obligations: Prove that for quasi-separated X and E in D_QCoh, tor amplitude of E in [a,b] is equivalent to the vanishing of H^i(E tensor F) outside [a,b] for all quasi-coherent F
proof_roadmap: The forward direction is immediate from the definition of tor amplitude

For the converse, take an affine etale j : U to X; assumption (2) applied to j_*G gives vanishing after pullback to U for E|_U tensor j^*j_*G, and since G is a direct summand of j^*j_*G by the etale pull-push splitting lemma, the vanishing holds against every quasi-coherent G on U, reducing to the representable case
For X a scheme, the small-etale comparison identifies E with epsilon^*E_0; flatness of epsilon transports the tensor vanishing between X and the scheme X_0, so the criterion on schemes applies
difficulty_reason: H2: a reduction argument through etale neighbourhoods and direct summands, then the schemes criterion; all steps written out.
